thread:
support-team: FYI — Acme reported p99 spikes this morning, repeatedly failing SLA. Customer attached trace ids and a screenshot of the dashboard (https://grafana/redwood/acme/latency). They say p95 looks OK but p99 is terrible. Can SRE take?
support-team: They mentioned this started after the runtime rollout at 03:10 UTC.
devon: On it. quick question — is the dashboard using histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)) or a native p99 from our rollup?
alex: It's histogram_quantile. That's what the dashboard panel uses.
mira: histogram_quantile can be sensitive to bucket boundaries. If we changed bucket scheme in the new runtime build, that could cause apparent p99 jumps even if tail behavior didn't change.
jules: Also remember we changed default aggregation window from 1m -> 5m in the runtime to reduce cardinality. That can hide short spikes or, conversely, amplify quantile calc depending on sample distribution.
metrics-bot: Alert: p99_latency_acme >= 1500ms for 3m (fired)
devon: Repro steps I'm running locally: hitting staging with ab -c50 -n2000 against the same model route; collecting /metrics snapshot before/after rollout. Will paste diffs.
(devon pasted)
```
# promql we used to query
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_latency_bucket{route="/v1/generate",env="prod"}[5m])) by (le))
# alternative raw approach
quantile_over_time(0.99, redwood_request_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])
```

alex: If the runtime switched to HDR histograms for internal aggregation and we expose classic prometheus buckets, we might have mismatch. Did the build change metric exporter?
mira: Build note: exporter bumped to v1.4.3 — we added high-cardinality labels removal and switched buckets to coarser powers-of-two up to 8s. There we go.
support-team: Customer says p95 remains ~120ms but p99 jumped to ~1800ms after the rollout. They provided example request ids in their ticket: rid:acme-2026-03-14-09a, acme-2026-03-14-09b.
devon: I pulled traces — those request ids show elevated backend_decode times ~1.6s on a single worker that handled a 2k-token prompt. Not all pods show it. Looks like a regression on a small subset of nodes.
jules: Could be a kernel-level affinity change with the new runtime affecting large sequence workloads. We saw a perf diff in the benchmark suite but thought it was noise.
ops-bot: Deploy 2026.03.14-03:08 rolled to cluster: inference-prod-7 (nodes: g4dn-8x)
alex: inference-prod-7 is the cluster that had the runtime change staged first. Suggest immediate mitigations: 1) cordon/evict pods on prod-7 and shift traffic to prod-3/4 2) rollback runtime to 2026.03.09 build 1.2.8 3) enable per-route fallback to smaller model variant for acme temporarily.
mira: Agree. Also add a temporary dashboard panel showing raw bucket counts for the slow nodes: sum by (instance,le) (rate(redwood_request_latency_bucket{route="/v1/generate",job="inference",instance=~"prod-7.*"}[1m]))
devon: I'll run a quick canary to validate rollback fixes. Running ab against one node now.
devon: Canary results: before rollback (runtime 1.3.0) single-node p99 ~1.65s for 2k-token tests; after rollback to 1.2.8 p99 dropped to 140ms. Repro is solid.
support-team: Customer replied they've seen intermittent errors too: 503s correlated with node OOMs? They exported pod logs showing OOMKilled for worker-3 on prod-7.
jules: Runtime 1.3.0 changed default max_batch_size for long requests and memory accounting. If max_batch_size grows unexpectedly, worker can OOM on long sequences. That would both cause OOMKills and long latencies during GC/eviction.
alex: Proposal: rollback runtime on prod-7 now, then revert max_batch_size change in master and run canary. I'll open a PR to explicitly set max_batch_size per-instance to a safe default and add a guard to the autoscaler to avoid packing long-sequence jobs into same GPU.
mira: For observability: we should stop relying only on histogram_quantile across aggregated buckets. Add per-instance p99 computed from raw summaries and a stitched panel that uses topk by instance then quantile_over_time to spot if one node is toxic. Quick promql draft: topk(5, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (instance,le) (rate(redwood_request_latency_bucket[1m]))))
devon: Also add an annotation to the grafana panel for the rollout at 03:10 so customers/internal teams can correlate.
support-team: Customer says they need a short RCA and temporary credits for the outage window. Can we provide an ETA?
ajex: (typo) alex: ETA for rollback + validation is 18 minutes. After that we'll collect root cause traces and put together a short postmortem.
mira: Action items I'm tracking: - rollback prod-7 runtime (in progress) - add per-instance p99 panel and raw bucket panel - open PR to pin max_batch_size + autoscaler guard - run data compare: export bucket manifests pre/post rollout
jules: I'll take the postmortem writeup draft once we have logs and the PRs linked. Will include reproducible steps and promql snippets.
metrics-bot: Note: Saved datasnapshot: /snapshots/1901234567-prod7-before.json
(devon) - rollback complete on prod-7, re-routing traffic -> prod-3/4. Initial customer p99 numbers trending down.
support-team: Customer confirmed latency dropped for a sample of requests. They still want forensic traces for the specific request ids.
devon: Attaching traces: 
```
# trace example
span: parse_input 30ms
span: model_decode 1600ms (on worker-3)
span: gc/paging 900ms
```

mira: Root cause summary (prelim): runtime exporter change altered histogram bucket granularity + new default max_batch_size allowed large long-sequence requests to be co-scheduled -> occasional OOMs and long GC/paging stalls on subset of nodes -> manifests as p99 spike in histogram_quantile and real p99 regressions for affected requests.
alex: Customer-facing note ready: "We identified a regression introduced in runtime build 1.3.0 affecting a subset of inference nodes that caused intermittent long tail latency and OOMs for long-sequence requests. We rolled back the rollout on affected nodes and implemented mitigations. We'll follow up with a full RCA and code fix timeline."
support-team: I'll send that and offer 4 hours of account credit for the window.
jules: After action: we should standardize on exposing summary metrics (direct p50/p95/p99) in addition to buckets, or ensure buckets are unchanged between builds. Also add a test in CI that runs histogram_quantile comparison for a few synthetic tails across builds.
mira: Agreed. Adding to roadmap: add histogram bucket backwards-compat check to the runtime release pipeline.
support-team: Thanks team — great response. Marking thread resolved when we have the postmortem link.
metrics-bot: Postmortem created: https://confluence/redwood/postmortems/1901234567-runtime-tail-regression
